editorial:
Imagine a small-time crook and a nerdy computer whiz trying to score a huge payday. That is exactly how things start for Antony Yakuza and Anwar. They think they have a solid plan for a big heist, but everything changes when they hire a quiet driver named Rejimon. At first, it feels like your typical crime caper with some funny banter and tense moments, but the vibe shifts quickly. You will feel the mood change as the movie stops being a simple robbery story and starts playing with your head, making you wonder what is actually real and what is just a trick of the mind.

The acting is top-notch, especially the chemistry between the nervous programmer and the tough gangster. The twists come out of nowhere and keep you glued to your seat, though some of the middle parts feel a bit slow. If you love movies that keep you guessing, you need to see this. For the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the weird visual effects, or rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your shelf is a great move.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you discover that Rejimon is actually a supernatural being who can bend time and space. The heist was never about the money, but a test to see if Antony and Anwar could trust each other. Once the twist hits, the world literally folds in on itself. Rejimon resets the timeline, giving the duo a second chance at life, but they keep their memories of the chaos they went through.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heist movies with a supernatural twist.
